Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the support so far — the pilot has been productive and the team wants a short runway to finish the final integration tests (about 3 weeks). Two quick asks from our side: 

1) Can Redwood either (A) issue an invoice now for a top-up (we'll pay Net 30) or (B) provide a credit voucher applied to our account balance? We prefer an invoice for org accounting, but open to credits if there's a conversion benefit to a committed purchase.

Samir — thanks for the clear ask and the report. Short answers up front: invoice (Net 30) is doable, and we can also issue a credit voucher if that is easier for your accounting. A few details to help you pick: 

- Invoice top-up (recommended for your procurement): Redwood generates a one-time invoice for the agreed top-up amount, payable Net 30. If you convert to a Dedicated or an annual committed package within 90 days, we can credit up to 30% of that invoice back toward the committed capacity (credit applied to future usage).

- Credit voucher: We can place an account-level credit that draws down against hosted usage. Credits can't be refunded and are not typically convertible to committed capacity, but they avoid PO/invoice cycles and clear faster on your books.

SLA/ops: For a short 3-week runway we can commit to the hosted service latency SLOs in our standard pilot addendum: 95th percentile response time target of 450ms for typical generative requests (with a backup fallback to a slightly higher-latency variant if spikes occur). We will provide a short engineering runbook and a dedicated escalation channel for this window. If you need a stricter latency number we can discuss a temporary Dedicated capacity add-on (higher cost) for the extension.

I've attached a worksheet that shows how the invoice/credit choices look against your current burn (Stratus_TopUp_Worksheet.xlsx). If you confirm the amount and preferred billing path, I'll draft a SOW amendment and loop finance/legal.

Thanks — Michael
Michael Grant
